title.zh: 卷五十九 吳書十四 吳主五子傳
title.en: Volume 59: Book of Wu 14 - Biographies of the five sons of the Lord of Wu
title.raw: 卷五十九 吳書十四 吳主五子傳 Volume 59: Book of Wu 14 - Biographies of the five sons of the Lord of Wu

sentences.zh: 孫登字子高，權長子也。

translations.literal: Sun Deng, courtesy name Zigao, was the eldest son of Sun Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Deng, whose courtesy name was Zigao, was Sun Quan's firstborn son.

sentences.zh: 魏黃初二年，以權爲吳王，拜登東中郎將，封萬戶侯，登辭疾不受。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangchu of Wei, Sun Quan was made King of Wu; Sun Deng was appointed General of the Household for All Purposes of the East and enfeoffed as marquis of ten thousand households, but Sun Deng declined citing illness and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In 221, the Wei court invested Sun Quan as King of Wu and named Sun Deng General of the Household for All Purposes of the East with a fief of ten thousand households; Sun Deng pleaded ill health and refused the appointment and title.

sentences.zh: 是歲，立登爲太子，選置師傅，銓簡秀士，以爲賔友，於是諸葛恪、張休、顧譚、陳表等以選入，侍講詩書，出從騎射。

translations.literal: That year he was established as heir apparent; masters and tutors were chosen and set in place, and outstanding scholars were screened and selected to be guests and companions; thereupon Zhuge Ke, Zhang Xiu, Gu Tan, Chen Biao, and others entered by selection, lecturing him on the Classics and histories indoors and accompanying him in riding and archery when he went out.
translations.idiomatic: The same year Sun Deng was made crown prince. Tutors were appointed and talented men chosen as his companions, so Zhuge Ke, Zhang Xiu, Gu Tan, Chen Biao, and others joined his household by competitive selection—indoors they expounded the Classics; outdoors they rode and shot with him.

sentences.zh: 權欲登讀《漢書》，習知近代之事，以張昭有師法，重煩勞之，乃令休從昭受讀，還以授登。

translations.literal: Sun Quan wished Sun Deng to read the Han shu and become familiar with affairs of recent times; because Zhang Zhao had proper methods of instruction and Sun Quan shrank from wearying him excessively, he ordered Zhang Xiu to receive instruction in reading from Zhang Zhao and return to teach Sun Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan wanted his heir to read the Han shu and learn recent history. Zhang Zhao was the acknowledged master teacher, but Sun Quan hesitated to burden him, so he had Zhang Xiu study under Zhang Zhao and then pass the lessons on to Sun Deng.

sentences.zh: 登待接寮屬，略用布衣之禮，與恪、休、譚等或同輿而載，或共帳而寐。

translations.literal: In receiving his subordinate officials Sun Deng broadly used the rites of a commoner, and with Ke, Xiu, Tan, and others he sometimes rode in the same carriage or slept in the same tent.
translations.idiomatic: With his staff Sun Deng kept to plain, almost commoner-level courtesy: he shared a carriage with Zhuge Ke, Zhang Xiu, Gu Tan, and the like, or slept in the same tent with them.

sentences.zh: 太傅張溫言於權曰：「夫中庶子官最親密，切問近對，宜用儁德。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Zhang Wen spoke to Sun Quan, saying: "The office of palace attendant is the most intimate; it answers pressing questions at close quarters; outstanding virtue ought to be employed."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Zhang Wen urged Sun Quan: "Palace attendants stand closest to the heir; they field urgent questions at his side. The posts demand men of exceptional moral stature."

sentences.zh: 」於是乃用表等爲中庶子。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Chen Biao and others were employed as palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan then appointed Chen Biao and others palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 後又以庶子禮拘，復令整巾侍坐。

translations.literal: Later, because the rites for palace attendants were restrictive, he again ordered them to arrange their headcloths and attend seated.
translations.idiomatic: Later the formal etiquette for attendants proved awkwardly stiff, so he told them to straighten their caps and take seats while on duty.

sentences.zh: 黃龍元年，權稱尊號，登爲皇太子，以恪爲左輔，休右弼，譚爲輔正，表爲翼正都尉，是爲四友，而謝景、范慎、刁玄、羊衜等皆爲賔客，

translations.literal: In the first year of Huanglong, when Sun Quan assumed the exalted title, Sun Deng became imperial heir; Ke was made left support, Xiu right support, Tan rectifier of the heir, Biao capital commandant who wings the rectifier—these were called the Four Friends—while Xie Jing, Fan Shen, Diao Xuan, Yang Dao, and others all became guests,
translations.idiomatic: In 229 Sun Quan took the imperial style; Sun Deng became crown prince. Zhuge Ke was named left support, Zhang Xiu right support, Gu Tan rectifier of the heir, and Chen Biao capital commandant who wings the rectifier—the group known as the Four Friends—while Xie Jing, Fan Shen, Diao Xuan, Yang Dao, and others served as his guests.

sentences.zh: 〈衜音道。〉

translations.literal: ( The note glosses the character as pronounced dao, like the word for 'way.' )
translations.idiomatic: ( The gloss reads the character with the same sound as dao, 'way.' )

sentences.zh: 於是東宮號爲多士。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Eastern Palace was styled as abounding in worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: The heir's establishment was soon renowned for the density of talent around him.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳錄》曰：慎字孝敬，廣陵人，竭忠知己之君，纏綿三益之友，時人榮之。

translations.literal: ( The Wu lu states: Fan, courtesy name Xiaojing, was a man of Guangling; he exhausted loyalty toward a ruler who knew him, and clung to friends who brought the three benefits; people of the time honored him for it. )
translations.idiomatic: ( According to the Wu lu, Fan Shen, styled Xiaojing, came from Guangling. He gave his whole loyalty to a sovereign who truly knew him, and he clung to friendships that enriched character in the classical "three ways"—contemporaries held him in high esteem. )

sentences.zh: 著論二十篇，名曰《矯非》。

translations.literal: He composed twenty treatises, entitled Rectifying Error.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote twenty essays collected under the title Rectifying Error.

sentences.zh: 後爲侍中，出補武昌左部督，治軍整頓。

translations.literal: Later he became palace attendant, went out to fill the post of commander of the left division at Wuchang, and governed the army in good order.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as palace attendant, then transferred to command the left wing at Wuchang, where he ran a tight, disciplined camp.

sentences.zh: 孫皓移都，甚憚之，詔曰：「慎勳德俱茂，朕所敬憑，宜登上公，以副衆望。

translations.literal: When Sun Hao moved the capital he greatly feared him and issued an edict saying: "Fan's merit and virtue are both flourishing; he is one on whom We rely in reverence; he ought to be raised to the highest duke rank to answer the hopes of the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Hao shifted the capital he grew wary of Fan Shen's stature and issued an edict: "Fan's achievements and character alike command respect; I lean on him with reverence. He should be promoted to grand preceptor to satisfy public expectation."

sentences.zh: 」以爲太尉。

translations.literal: He was made grand commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 慎自恨久爲將，遂託老耄。

translations.literal: Fan Shen himself resented having long been a general and therefore pleaded extreme old age.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shen had wearied of life in the field and pleaded senility to step down.

sentences.zh: 軍士戀之，舉營爲之隕涕。

translations.literal: The soldiers were attached to him; the whole camp wept tears for him.
translations.idiomatic: The troops loved him; an entire camp shed tears at his departure.

sentences.zh: 鳳凰三年卒，子耀嗣。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Fenghuang; his son Yao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 274; his son Fan Yao inherited his rank.

sentences.zh: 玄，丹楊人。

translations.literal: Xuan was a man of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Xuan was from Danyang.

sentences.zh: 衜，南陽人。

translations.literal: Dao was a man of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dao came from Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 《吳書》曰：衜初爲中庶子，年二十。

translations.literal: The Wu shu states: Dao at first was a palace attendant; he was twenty years of age.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu shu records that Yang Dao began as a palace attendant at the age of twenty.

sentences.zh: 時廷尉監隱蕃交結豪傑，自衞將軍全琮等皆傾心敬待，惟衜及宣詔郎豫章楊迪拒絕不與通，時人咸怪之。

translations.literal: At that time the jail overseer of the commandant of justice, Yin Fan, cultivated ties with bold spirits; from Guard General Quan Zong downward all inclined their hearts and treated him with respect; only Dao and the edict announcer of Yuzhang, Yang Di, refused and would not associate with him; people of the time all thought it strange.
translations.idiomatic: The court jailer Yin Fan was courting powerful men, and even Guard General Quan Zong courted his favor—yet Yang Dao and the edict herald Yang Di of Yuzhang would have nothing to do with him, which contemporaries found inexplicable.

sentences.zh: 而蕃後叛逆，衆乃服之。

translations.literal: But when Fan later rebelled, the crowd then admired them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Fan later turned traitor, everyone conceded that Yang Dao and Yang Di had been right.

sentences.zh: 《江表傳》曰：登使侍中胡綜作賔友目曰：「英才卓越，超踰倫匹，則諸葛恪。

translations.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states: Deng ordered Palace Attendant Hu Zong to compose a catalogue of guests and companions, saying: "In outstanding talent that transcends the common run, surpassing peers, there is Zhuge Ke."
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan says Sun Deng had Palace Attendant Hu Zong draft appraisals of his companions: "For brilliance that towers above ordinary men, there is Zhuge Ke."

sentences.zh: 精識時機，達幽究微，則顧譚。

translations.literal: In keen perception of the opportune moment, penetrating the obscure and investigating the subtle, there is Gu Tan.
translations.idiomatic: For sharp judgment of timing and insight into hidden motives, there is Gu Tan.

sentences.zh: 凝辨宏達，言能釋結，則謝景。

translations.literal: In concentrated discernment and breadth of vision, in speech able to unravel knots, there is Xie Jing.
translations.idiomatic: For steady judgment, breadth of mind, and words that untangle dilemmas, there is Xie Jing.

sentences.zh: 究學甄微，游夏同科，則范慎。

translations.literal: In exhaustive study and discrimination of the subtle, on a par with You and Xia, there is Fan Shen.
translations.idiomatic: For scholarship that sifts the fine points and rivals the disciples You and Xia, there is Fan Shen.

sentences.zh: 」衜乃私駁綜曰：「元遜才而疏，子嘿精而狠，叔發辯而浮，孝敬深而狹。

translations.literal: " Dao then privately refuted Zong, saying: "Yuanxun has talent but is careless; Zimo is acute but harsh; Shufa is eloquent but shallow; Xiaojing is profound but narrow.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Dao quietly contradicted Hu Zong: "Zhuge Ke is gifted but careless; Gu Tan is sharp but ruthless; Xie Jing is fluent but shallow; Fan Shen is deep but narrow-minded.

sentences.zh: 」所言皆有指趣。

translations.literal: " What he said all had pointed significance.
translations.idiomatic: " Each remark had a clear point behind it.

sentences.zh: 而衜卒以此言見咎，不爲恪等所親。

translations.literal: But Dao in the end because of these words incurred blame and was not treated as intimate by Ke and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Those words earned Yang Dao resentment, and Zhuge Ke's circle never warmed to him.

sentences.zh: 後四人皆敗，吳人謂衜之言有徵。

translations.literal: Later when the four men all met ruin, the people of Wu said Dao's words had been verified.
translations.idiomatic: When all four later fell, Wu observers said Yang Dao's verdicts had proved prophetic.

sentences.zh: 位至桂陽太守，卒。〉

translations.literal: He rose to the rank of administrator of Guiyang and died. )
translations.idiomatic: He rose to prefect of Guiyang and died there. )

sentences.zh: 權遷都建業，徵上大將軍陸遜輔登鎮武昌，領宮府留事。

translations.literal: Sun Quan moved the capital to Jianye, summoned Grand Senior General Lu Xun to assist Deng in garrisoning Wuchang, and charged him with the remaining affairs of the palace establishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan relocated the court to Jianye, he recalled Lu Xun from the field to help Sun Deng hold Wuchang and oversee all residual business of the heir's establishment.

sentences.zh: 登或射獵，當由徑道，常遠避良田，不踐苗稼，至所頓息，又擇空閑之地，其不欲煩民如此。

translations.literal: When Deng at times hunted, if he had to take a path he constantly kept far from good fields, not treading on seedlings and crops; when he came to a place to halt and rest, he again chose empty idle ground; his not wishing to trouble the people was like this.
translations.idiomatic: On the hunt he kept to byways and gave wide berth to fertile plots so as never to trample crops; when he camped he picked unused ground—such was his care not to burden commoners.

sentences.zh: 嘗乘馬出，有彈丸過，左右求之。

translations.literal: Once when riding out on horseback, a pellet passed by; his attendants searched for the shooter.
translations.idiomatic: Once, riding out, a sling pellet whistled past; his escorts set out to find who had fired it.

sentences.zh: 有一人操彈佩丸，咸以爲是，辭對不服，從者欲捶之，登不聽，使求過丸，比之非類，乃見釋。

translations.literal: There was one man who held a pellet-launcher and wore pellets; all thought it was he; he pleaded and answered that he would not submit; the followers wished to beat him; Deng would not listen; he had them seek the passing pellet; comparing it, it was not of the same kind, and only then was the man released.
translations.idiomatic: They seized a man carrying a sling and pellets and assumed he was guilty; he protested his innocence until the escort wanted to thrash him. Sun Deng forbade it, had the actual pellet recovered, and showed it did not match the man's shot—so he was freed.

sentences.zh: 又失盛水金馬盂，覺得其主，左右所爲，不忍致罰，呼責數之，長遣歸家，勑親近勿言。

translations.literal: Again he lost a gold horse-head water basin; he perceived who the owner was—it was done by those at his side; he could not bear to impose punishment; he called and rebuked them at length, sent them home for a long period, and ordered those close to him not to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: When a gilt horse-head basin went missing, he traced it to his own attendants. He could not bring himself to punish them: he scolded them at length, sent them home on extended leave, and told his intimates to keep silent about the affair.

sentences.zh: 後弟慮卒，權爲之降損，登晝夜兼行，到賴鄉，自聞，即時召見。

translations.literal: Later when his younger brother Lu died, Sun Quan for his sake lowered and diminished rites; Deng traveled day and night together, arrived at Laixiang, reported himself on hearing the news, and was immediately summoned and received.
translations.idiomatic: After his brother Sun Lü died, Sun Quan curtailed court observances in grief. Sun Deng rode night and day to Laixiang, presented himself unbidden, and was admitted at once.

sentences.zh: 見權悲泣，因諫曰：「慮寢疾不起，此乃命也。

translations.literal: Seeing Sun Quan he wept in grief and therefore remonstrated, saying: "Lü lay ill and did not rise; this is fate."
translations.idiomatic: He found his father in tears and urged him: "Sun Lü's illness ran its course—that was heaven's decree."

sentences.zh: 方今朔土未一，四海喁喁，天戴陛下，而以下流之念，減損大官殽饌，過於禮制，臣竊憂惶。

translations.literal: At present the northern lands are not unified; within the four seas all look upward; Heaven bears up Your Majesty; yet because of thoughts flowing downstream you reduce and diminish the meats and viands of the great kitchen, exceeding the regulations of ritual; your servant privately is anxious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: The north is still unconquered; the realm hangs on your every word. Yet grief has led you to cut back the imperial kitchen beyond what ritual allows—I cannot help but worry.

sentences.zh: 」權納其言，爲之加膳。

translations.literal: Sun Quan accepted his words and for his sake increased the viands.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan took the point and restored fuller meals.

sentences.zh: 住十餘日，欲遣西還，深自陳乞，以乆離定省，子道有闕，又陳陸遜忠勤，無所顧憂，權遂留焉。

translations.literal: He stayed more than ten days; Sun Quan wished to send him back west; he deeply stated his own plea that, having long been separated from fixed attendance, there was a gap in the way of a son; he also stated that Lu Xun was loyal and diligent and there was nothing to worry over in looking after affairs; Sun Quan thereupon kept him.
translations.idiomatic: After ten days Sun Quan meant to send him back to the western command, but Sun Deng begged to stay: he had long neglected his filial duty of visiting his parents, he said, and Lu Xun was loyal and diligent enough that the western front needed no further anxiety from the heir. Sun Quan let him remain.

sentences.zh: 嘉禾三年，權征新城，使登居守，總知留事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiahe, Sun Quan campaigned against Xincheng and ordered Deng to remain in guard and overall manage remaining affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 234, when Sun Quan marched on Xincheng, he left Sun Deng in charge at the capital with full authority over rear-area administration.

sentences.zh: 時年穀不豐，頗有盜賊，乃表定科令，所以防禦，甚得止姦之要。

translations.literal: At that time the year's grain was not abundant and there were quite a few bandits; he therefore submitted a memorial fixing statutes and ordinances for purposes of defense, and grasped very well the essentials of stopping wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Harvests were poor and banditry common, so he memorialized for codified regulations on defense and hit exactly the measures needed to curb crime.

sentences.zh: 初，登所生庶賤，徐夫人少有母養之恩，後徐氏以妬廢處吳，而步夫人最寵。

translations.literal: At first, the one who bore Deng was of lowly common birth; Lady Xu the consort had once had the grace of mothering him in his youth; later the Xu clan because of jealousy was deposed and dwelt in Wu, while Lady Bu the consort was most favored.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Deng's birth mother had been a woman of humble station. Lady Xu had raised him briefly in his childhood, but she was later cast aside for jealousy and sent to live in Wu, while Consort Lady Bu became Sun Quan's favorite.

sentences.zh: 步氏有賜，登不敢辭，拜受而已。

translations.literal: When the Bu clan had gifts, Deng did not dare decline; he bowed and received only.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Bu sent gifts he did not dare refuse them—he merely bowed and accepted.

sentences.zh: 徐氏使至，所賜衣服，必沐浴服之。

translations.literal: When the Xu clan's messenger arrived, for clothing that was bestowed he invariably bathed before donning it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Lady Xu sent clothing, he bathed before putting it on, treating her gifts with full ritual respect.

sentences.zh: 登將拜太子，辭曰：「本立而道生，欲立太子，宜先立后。

translations.literal: When Deng was about to be invested as heir apparent, he declined, saying: "When the root is established then the Way is born; if one wishes to establish the heir apparent, one ought first to establish the empress."
translations.idiomatic: As he was to be named heir, he objected: "The Analects say, 'When the root is firm, the Way grows.' If you mean to name a crown prince, you should first name an empress."

sentences.zh: 」權曰：「卿母安在？

translations.literal: " Sun Quan said: "Where is your mother?
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan asked, "Where is your mother now?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「在吳。

translations.literal: " He replied: "She is in Wu.
translations.idiomatic: " "In Wu," he answered.

sentences.zh: 」權嘿然。

translations.literal: " Sun Quan was silent.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan said nothing.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：弟和有寵於權，登親敬，待之如兄，常有欲讓之心。〉

translations.literal: ( The Wu shu states: His younger brother He had favor with Sun Quan; Deng treated him with intimacy and respect, treating him as an elder brother, and constantly had a mind to yield to him. )
translations.idiomatic: ( The Wu shu adds that his younger brother Sun He enjoyed Sun Quan's favor; Sun Deng honored him almost as an elder and more than once thought of yielding the succession to him. )

sentences.zh: 立凡二十一年，年三十三卒。

translations.literal: Having been established in all twenty-one years, at age thirty-three he died.
translations.idiomatic: He had been heir for twenty-one years when he died at thirty-three.

sentences.zh: 臨終，上疏曰：「臣以無狀，嬰抱篤疾，自省微劣，懼卒隕斃。

translations.literal: At the end of his life he submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant, lacking good form, has been encircled by grave illness; examining himself, he is slight and inferior and fears he will suddenly perish."
translations.idiomatic: Near death he addressed a memorial: "I have conducted myself without distinction and now lie gravely ill; knowing my own slight worth, I fear I may suddenly be taken."

sentences.zh: 臣不自惜，念當委離供養，埋胔后土，長不復奉望宮省，朝覲日月，生無益於國，死貽陛下重慼，以此爲哽結耳。

translations.literal: Your servant does not pity himself, but thinks that he must cast off support and bury his flesh in the earth below, long not again to gaze on the palace precincts or court the sun and moon; in life he was of no benefit to the state, in death he leaves Your Majesty heavy grief—on this account it knots his throat.
translations.idiomatic: It is not my own fate I mourn, but that I must leave your service and lie beneath the soil, never again to attend court or behold your radiance. I have done the state little good in life, and my death will only deepen your sorrow—that is what chokes me.

sentences.zh: 臣聞死生有命，長短自天，周晉、顏回有上智之才，而尚夭折，況臣愚陋，年過其壽，生爲國嗣，沒享榮祚，於臣已多，亦何悲恨哉！

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that death and life have their allotment and length and brevity come from Heaven; the kings of Zhou and Jin and Yan Hui had talents of the highest wisdom, yet still met early death—how much more your servant, stupid and mean, his years having passed his allotted span, who in life was heir of the state and in death will enjoy glorious fortune—for your servant it is already much; what grief or resentment is there!
translations.idiomatic: I know life and death are decreed and longevity is heaven's gift. The Zhou and Jin kings and Yan Hui were men of supreme intellect, yet they died young—how much more I, dull and obscure, who have already outlived my share, lived as your heir, and will depart with honors few could claim? What room is left for regret?

sentences.zh: 方今大事未定，逋寇未討，萬國喁喁，係命陛下，危者望安，亂者仰治。

translations.literal: At present the great matter is not settled, the fugitive foe is not punished; the myriad regions murmur with upturned mouths; their lives hang on Your Majesty; those in peril look to be secured, those in disorder look up to be governed.
translations.idiomatic: The great enterprise is unfinished; rebels still roam. Every corner of the realm looks to you for its very breath—the imperiled seek safety, the chaotic seek order.

sentences.zh: 願陛下棄忘臣身，割下流之恩，脩黃老之術，篤養神光，加羞珍膳，廣開神明之慮，以定無窮之業，則率土幸賴，臣死無恨也。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to cast off and forget your servant's person, cut away the favor that flows downstream, cultivate the arts of Huang and Lao, earnestly nurture the spirit's radiance, increase and bring forth rare viands, broadly open the considerations of spirit-like clarity, so as to settle the enterprise without end—then within the bounds of the earth all will happily rely, and your servant in death will have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: Forget me, I beg you; set aside grief's pull. Practice the quieting arts of Huang-Lao, cherish your vital spirit, take rich nourishment, and broaden your mind for the boundless work ahead. If the realm can lean on you thus, I shall die content.

sentences.zh: 皇子和仁孝聦哲，德行清茂，宜早建置，以繫民望。

translations.literal: The imperial son He is humane, filial, keen, and wise; his virtue and conduct are pure and flourishing; he ought early to be established and set in place so as to tie the hopes of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Prince He is humane, filial, and quick of mind; his character is bright and sound. Establish him soon to answer what the people expect.

sentences.zh: 諸葛恪才略博達，器任佐時。

translations.literal: Zhuge Ke's talent and strategy are broad and comprehensive; his capacity fits assisting the age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke combines breadth of talent with strategic depth—he has the capacity to serve the times.

sentences.zh: 張休、顧譚、謝景，皆通敏有識斷，入宜委腹心，出可爲爪牙。

translations.literal: Zhang Xiu, Gu Tan, and Xie Jing are all penetrating and quick and have judgment; within they may be entrusted as heart and belly, without they can serve as claws and fangs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiu, Gu Tan, and Xie Jing are astute men of clear judgment—keep them at your breast in council, send them to the field as your strong arm.

sentences.zh: 范慎、華融矯矯壯節，有國士之風。

translations.literal: Fan Shen and Hua Rong, lofty and martial in integrity, have the bearing of men of state.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shen and Hua Rong carry themselves with the stern dignity of true "knights of the realm."

sentences.zh: 羊衜辯捷，有專對之材。

translations.literal: Yang Dao is eloquent and quick and has the talent for exclusive response.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dao is quick-witted and eloquent—material for embassies and set-piece debate.

sentences.zh: 刁玄優弘，志履道真。

translations.literal: Diao Xuan is generous and great; his intent treads the true Way.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Xuan is large-minded and steady, his aspirations rooted in what is genuine.

sentences.zh: 裴欽博記，翰采足用。

translations.literal: Pei Qin broadly remembers; his brush splendor suffices for employment.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Qin's memory is encyclopedic and his pen more than adequate to any task.

sentences.zh: 蔣脩、虞翻，志節分明。

translations.literal: Jiang Xiu and Yu Fan have aims and integrity that are clear and distinct.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xiu and Yu Fan are men of unmistakable principle.

sentences.zh: 凡此諸臣，或宜廊廟，或任將帥，皆練時事，明習法令，守信固義，有不可奪之志。

translations.literal: All these various ministers, some suitable for hall and temple, some fit to serve as generals and commanders, are all practiced in affairs of the times, clearly versed in statutes and ordinances, keep faith and solidify righteousness, and have aims that cannot be wrested away.
translations.idiomatic: Each of these men belongs either in the council chamber or at the head of an army. They know the business of government, the letter of the law, and the claims of honor—none of them is easily swayed from his purpose.

sentences.zh: 此皆陛下日月所照，選置臣宮，得與從事，備知情素，敢以陳聞。

translations.literal: These all are illumined by Your Majesty's sun and moon; chosen and set in your servant's palace, they obtained to work with him and your servant fully knows their dispositions and past conduct; he dares to set them forth for Your hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Your light has fallen on them all; they served in my household and I know their character through and through—I presume to commend them to you.

sentences.zh: 臣重惟當今方外多虞，師旅未休，當厲六軍，以圖進取。

translations.literal: Your servant further considers that at present beyond the borders there are many alarms, armies and hosts do not rest; one ought to sharpen the six armies to plan advance and seizure.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond our borders trouble still stirs and the armies never rest. Harden the host and press the advantage while you can.

sentences.zh: 軍以人爲衆，衆以財爲寶，竊聞郡縣頗有荒殘，民物凋弊，姦亂萌生，是以法令繁滋，刑辟重切。

translations.literal: Armies take men as their multitude, multitudes take wealth as their treasure; your servant has privately heard that commanderies and districts are in many places desolate and ruined, people and goods are withered and exhausted, treachery and disorder sprout and arise; for this reason statutes and ordinances multiply and thrive, punishments and penalties are heavy and keen.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers need men, and men need means. I hear that many districts lie waste, the people are exhausted, and crime is spreading—hence the thickening of laws and the severity of punishments.

sentences.zh: 臣聞爲政聽民，律令與時推移，誠宜與將相大臣詳擇時宜，博采衆議，寬刑輕賦，均息力役，以順民望。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that in governing one listens to the people; statutes and ordinances shift with the times; truly one ought with generals, ministers, and great officials carefully choose what fits the times, broadly gather the multitude's proposals, widen punishments and lighten levies, evenly still labor and corvée, so as to comply with the people's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Good government heeds the people; laws must move with the times. Counsel with your generals and ministers, gather opinion widely, ease penalties and taxes, and balance labor service—that is how to answer what the people long for.

sentences.zh: 陸遜忠勤於時，出身憂國，謇謇在公，有匪躬之節。

translations.literal: Lu Xun is loyal and diligent toward the times; he gives his person in worry for the state; he is outspoken in public service and has the integrity of not sparing his person.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun has been loyal and tireless, staking himself on the state's troubles and speaking plainly in its service—the classic minister who forgets self for duty.

sentences.zh: 諸葛瑾、步隲、朱然、全琮、朱據、呂岱、吾粲、闞澤、嚴畯、張承、孫怡忠於爲國，通達治體。

translations.literal: Zhuge Jin, Bu Zhi, Zhu Ran, Quan Zong, Zhu Ju, Lü Dai, Wu Can, Kan Ze, Yan Jun, Zhang Cheng, and Sun Yi are loyal in acting for the state and comprehend the body of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Jin, Bu Zhi, Zhu Ran, Quan Zong, Zhu Ju, Lü Dai, Wu Can, Kan Ze, Yan Jun, Zhang Cheng, and Sun Yi are steadfast servants of the state who understand how government works.

sentences.zh: 可令陳上便宜，蠲除苛煩，愛養士馬，撫循百姓。

translations.literal: They may be ordered to set forth what is advantageous, remit and remove harsh vexations, cherish and nurture soldiers and horses, comfort and follow the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Charge them to memorialize on practical reforms, strip away vexatious exactions, care for troops and horses, and soothe the common people.

sentences.zh: 五年之外，十年之內，遠者歸復，近者盡力，兵不血刃，而大事可定也。

translations.literal: Beyond five years, within ten years, those far will return and restore themselves, those near will exhaust their strength, arms will not blood blades, and the great matter can be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Within five to ten years the distant will rally, the near will give their all, and you may settle the great enterprise without drawing a sword.

sentences.zh: 臣聞『鳥之將死其鳴也哀，人之將死其言也善』，故子囊臨終，遺言戒時，君子以爲忠，豈況臣登，其能已乎？

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that 'when a bird is about to die its cry is mournful; when a man is about to die his words are good'; therefore when Zi-nang faced the end, his dying words warned the times, and the gentleman deemed it loyalty—how much more your servant Deng, could he stop himself?
translations.idiomatic: They say a dying bird's cry is sad and a dying man's words are true. Zi-nang's deathbed counsel was judged loyal by every gentleman—how could I, Sun Deng, fall silent?

sentences.zh: 願陛下留意聽采，臣雖死之日，猶生之年也。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to heed and listen and gather them in; though it be the day of your servant's death, it is still as the years of his life.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to weigh these words: the day I die will still be a day I have lived, if you hear me.

sentences.zh: 」旣絕而後書聞，權益以摧感，言則隕涕。

translations.literal: After he had expired, only then was the memorial heard; Sun Quan all the more was crushed and moved, and when he spoke tears fell.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial reached Sun Quan only after Sun Deng had died. Sun Quan was shattered; whenever he spoke of it, he wept.

sentences.zh: 是歲，赤烏四年也。

translations.literal: That year was the fourth year of Chiwu.
translations.idiomatic: It was the fourth year of the Chiwu era (241).

sentences.zh: 謝景時爲豫章太守，不勝哀情，棄官奔赴，拜表自劾。

translations.literal: Xie Jing at the time was administrator of Yuzhang; unable to overcome grief, he cast aside office and hurried to attend; he submitted a memorial impeaching himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jing was prefect of Yuzhang. Overcome by grief, he abandoned his post to hurry to the capital and memorialized for punishment.

sentences.zh: 權曰：「君與太子從事，異於他吏。

translations.literal: Sun Quan said: "You in serving the heir apparent differ from other officials."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan told him, "Your service to the heir sets you apart from ordinary officials."

sentences.zh: 」使中使慰勞，聽復本職，發遣還郡。

translations.literal: " He sent inner envoys to console and comfort him, permitted him to resume his original office, and issued orders sending him back to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent envoys to console Xie Jing, allowed him to resume his post, and sent him back to his commandery.

sentences.zh: 謚登曰宣太子。

translations.literal: Deng was given the posthumous title Expositor Heir.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Deng was canonized as Crown Prince Xuan ("the Expositor").

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：初葬句容，置園邑，奉守如法，後三年改葬蔣陵。〉

translations.literal: ( The Wu shu states: At first he was buried at Jurong, a park settlement was established, and guardianship was maintained according to law; after three years he was reburied at the Jiang Mausoleum by Bell Mountain. )
translations.idiomatic: ( The Wu shu records that he was first interred at Jurong with a funerary estate and guardians as statute required, then, three years later, moved to the Jiang Mausoleum near Zhongshan. )

sentences.zh: 子璠、希，皆早卒，次子英，封吳侯。

translations.literal: His sons Fan and Xi both died early; the second son Ying was enfeoffed as marquis of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Sun Fan and Sun Xi died young; the second son, Sun Ying, was enfeoffed as marquis of Wu.

sentences.zh: 五鳳元年，英以大將軍孫峻擅權，謀誅峻，事覺自殺，國除。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wufeng, Ying because Grand General Sun Jun monopolized power plotted to kill Jun; the affair was discovered and he committed suicide; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In 254 Sun Ying plotted to kill Grand General Sun Jun, who had seized power. The plot leaked; Sun Ying killed himself and his fief was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳歷》曰：孫和以無罪見殺，衆庶皆懷憤歎，前司馬桓慮因此招合將吏，欲共殺峻立英，事覺，皆見殺，英實不知。〉

translations.literal: ( The Wu li states: Because Sun He was killed though without guilt, the common multitude all harbored indignant sighs; the former major Huan Lu therefore assembled generals and clerks, wishing together to kill Jun and establish Ying; the affair was discovered and all were killed; Ying in truth did not know. )
translations.idiomatic: ( The Wu li relates that when Sun He was executed though innocent, popular resentment ran high. The former major Huan Lu rallied officers to kill Sun Jun and enthrone Sun Ying; when the plot was exposed they were all executed, and Sun Ying had known nothing of it. )

sentences.zh: 謝景者字叔發，南陽宛人。

translations.literal: Xie Jing, styled Shufa, was a man of Wan in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jing, courtesy name Shufa, was a native of Wan in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 在郡有治迹，吏民稱之，以爲前有顧劭，其次即景。

translations.literal: In the commandery he had traces of good rule; clerks and commoners praised him, considering that before there had been Gu Shao, and next after him was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect he left a record of good government; officials and people praised him, ranking him second only to the celebrated Gu Shao.

sentences.zh: 數年卒官。

translations.literal: After several years he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office a few years later.

sentences.zh: 孫慮字子智，登弟也。

translations.literal: Sun Lu, courtesy name Zizhi, was Deng's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lu, styled Zizhi, was Sun Deng's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 少敏惠有才藝，權器愛之。

translations.literal: In youth he was keen, clever, and had talents and arts; Sun Quan valued and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he showed quick intelligence and varied gifts; Sun Quan doted on him.

sentences.zh: 黃武七年，封建昌侯。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Huangwu he was enfeoffed as marquis of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: In 228 he received the title of marquis of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 後二年，丞相雍等奏慮性聦體達，所尚日新，比方近漢，宜進爵稱王，權未許。

translations.literal: After two years, Chancellor Yong and others memorialized that Lu by nature was intelligent, his person comprehensive, what he esteemed daily renewed, comparing him to the recent Han, he ought to advance in rank and be titled king; Sun Quan did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Chancellor Yong and others urged that Sun Lu was bright, well rounded, and ever improving—comparable to Han princes—and should be promoted to king. Sun Quan refused.

sentences.zh: 乆之，尚書僕射存上疏曰：「帝王之興，莫不襃崇至親，以光羣后，故魯衞於周，寵冠諸侯，高帝五王，封列于漢，所以藩屏本朝，爲國鎮衞。

translations.literal: After a long time, Vice Director of the Secretariat Cun submitted a memorial saying: "In the rise of emperors and kings there has never been one who did not exalt and honor the utmost kin so as to bring glory to the host of lords; therefore Lu and Wei toward Zhou had favor crowning the feudal lords, the five kings of the Exalted Founder were enfeoffed in array in the Han—these were the means to screen the root court and act as bulwarks and guards for the state."
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Vice Director of the Secretariat Cun memorialized: "Every founding house exalts its closest kin to shine on the nobility—Lu and Wei stood first among Zhou lords, and Gaozu's five princes secured the Han. Such kin are the screen around the throne and the state's shield."

sentences.zh: 建昌侯慮稟性聦敏，才兼文武，於古典制，宜正名號。

translations.literal: The marquis of Jianchang Lu by endowment is intelligent and keen, his talents embrace both civil and military; according to ancient classical regulations, he ought to have his name and title rectified.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Sun Lu of Jianchang is clever by nature and gifted in both civil and military affairs; classical precedent calls for his title to be regularized.

sentences.zh: 陛下謙光，未肯如舊，羣寮大小，咸用於邑。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's modest radiance has not been willing to follow the old pattern; hosts great and small among the host of officials all therefore are pent up.
translations.idiomatic: Your modesty has held you back from following precedent, and the whole bureaucracy is frustrated.

sentences.zh: 方今姦寇恣睢，金鼓未弭，腹心爪牙，惟親與賢。

translations.literal: At present treacherous foes act as they please; gongs and drums are not stilled; heart-belly and claws and fangs are only kin and worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels still swagger and the drums of war have not quieted. For the men at your breast and the arm you strike with, nothing matches kinsmen and proven talent.

sentences.zh: 輒與丞相雍等議，咸以慮宜爲鎮軍大將軍，授任偏方，以光大業。

translations.literal: We have then deliberated with Chancellor Yong and others; all consider that Lu ought to be made general who stabilizes the army, grant him appointment on a side quarter, so as to broaden and magnify the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: We have consulted Chancellor Yong and the rest: all agree that Sun Lu should be named general who stabilizes the army and given a regional command to magnify your great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 」權乃許之，於是假節開府，治半州。

translations.literal: " Sun Quan thereupon granted it; thereupon Lu was given credentials of authority and opened a general's headquarters, administering half the province.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan agreed. Sun Lü received the imperial baton, opened his own command, and governed half the province.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》載權詔曰：「期運擾亂，凶邪肆虐，威罰有序，干戈不戢。

translations.literal: ( The Wu shu records Sun Quan's edict: "The allotted span is troubled and chaotic; the vicious and wicked run rampant; awesome punishments have their order, yet arms are not laid down.
translations.idiomatic: ( The Wu shu preserves Sun Quan's edict: "Fortune's course is in turmoil and the wicked hold sway; though justice has its course, the weapons of war have not been stowed away.

sentences.zh: 以慮氣志休懿，武略夙昭，必能爲國佐定大業，故授以上將之位，至以殊特之榮，寵以兵馬之勢，委以偏方之任。

translations.literal: Because Lu in temper and intent is generous and fine, his martial strategy long manifest, he is sure to be able for the state to assist in settling the great enterprise, therefore We confer on him the position of chief general, reaching to the glory of singular distinction, favor him with the power of arms and horses, and entrust him with responsibility for a side quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lü's bearing is noble and his military talent proven—he can help secure the great work. So I invest him as a supreme general, grant him extraordinary honor, put troops at his disposal, and charge him with a frontier command.

sentences.zh: 外欲威振敵虜，厭難萬里，內欲鎮撫遠近，慰卹將士，誠慮建功立事竭命之秋也。

translations.literal: Without, We desire to awe and shake the enemy barbarians and crush hardship for ten thousand li; within, We desire to pacify and soothe far and near, console and relieve generals and soldiers—truly We consider this the autumn when Lu ought to exhaust his life in establishing merit and accomplishing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Without, he shall overawe the foe across a thousand miles; within, he shall steady the realm and hearten the army. This is the season for him to stake everything on achievement.

sentences.zh: 慮其內脩文德，外經武訓，持盈若沖，則滿而不溢。

translations.literal: Lu ought within to cultivate civil virtue, without to regulate martial training, hold fullness as if it were emptiness, then though full he will not overflow.
translations.idiomatic: Let him cultivate civil virtue within and drill the army without; let him keep a full measure as if it were still empty, so that success never spills into arrogance.

sentences.zh: 敬慎乃心，無忝所受。」〉

translations.literal: Be reverent and careful in your heart; do not disgrace what you have received." )
translations.idiomatic: Guard your heart with care, and do not shame the trust I place in you." )

sentences.zh: 慮以皇子之尊，富於春秋，遠近嫌其不能留意。

translations.literal: Lu, by the dignity of an imperial son, being rich in the spring and autumn of years, those near and far suspected that he could not attend to business with care.
translations.idiomatic: As a prince in the bloom of youth, he was thought too young to handle real responsibility.

sentences.zh: 及至臨事，遵奉法度，敬納師友，過於衆望。

translations.literal: But when it came to facing affairs, he observed and upheld the laws, respectfully received masters and friends, and exceeded the multitude's expectations.
translations.idiomatic: When power actually came to him, he followed statute, heeded his tutors, and surpassed what anyone had expected.

sentences.zh: 年二十，嘉禾元年卒。

translations.literal: At age twenty, in the first year of Jiahe, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 232, aged twenty.

sentences.zh: 無子，國除。

translations.literal: He had no son; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He left no heir, and the marquisate was abolished.

sentences.zh: 孫和字子孝，慮弟也。

translations.literal: Sun He, courtesy name Zixiao, was Lu's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Sun He, styled Zixiao, was Sun Lü's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 少以母王有寵見愛，年十四，爲置宮衞，使中書令闞澤教以書藝。

translations.literal: In youth because his mother Lady Wang had favor he was loved; at age fourteen a palace guard was established for him, and Sun Quan ordered Director of the Secretariat Kan Ze to teach him writing and arts.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Wang was in favor, so he was doted on from boyhood. At fourteen he received a princely guard, and Kan Ze of the Secretariat was ordered to tutor him in letters and the arts.

sentences.zh: 好學下士，甚見稱述。

translations.literal: He loved learning and humbled himself before scholars; he was much praised in report.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books and treated men of learning with deference, and won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 赤烏五年，立爲太子，時年十九。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chiwu he was established as heir apparent; at the time he was nineteen.
translations.idiomatic: In 242, at nineteen, he was named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 闞澤爲太傅，薛綜爲少傅，而蔡穎、張純、封俌、嚴維等皆從容侍從。

translations.literal: Kan Ze became grand tutor, Xue Zong junior tutor, while Cai Ying, Zhang Chun, Feng Fu, Yan Wei, and others all attended him at ease in following service.
translations.idiomatic: Kan Ze was made grand tutor and Xue Zong junior tutor; Cai Ying, Zhang Chun, Feng Fu, Yan Wei, and others formed his leisurely circle of attendants.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：和少岐嶷有智意，故權尤愛幸，常在左右，衣服禮秩雕玩珍異之賜，諸子莫得比焉。

translations.literal: ( The Wu shu states: He in youth was precocious and had intelligent purpose, therefore Sun Quan especially loved and favored him, constantly kept him at his right and left, and in gifts of clothing, ritual rank, carved playthings, and rare treasures none of the other sons could compare.
translations.idiomatic: ( The Wu shu says Sun He was precocious and clever, so Sun Quan favored him above the rest, kept him always at his side, and showered him with gifts no other son received.

sentences.zh: 好文學，善騎射，承師涉學，精識聦敏，尊敬師傅，愛好人物。

translations.literal: He loved literary learning, was good at riding and archery, received teachers and crossed into study, was keen in perception and quick and clever, respected masters and tutors, and loved and esteemed men of note.
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated literature, excelled at riding and archery, studied under masters, showed sharp wit, honored his tutors, and cherished worthy men.

sentences.zh: 穎等每朝見進賀，和常降意，歡以待之。

translations.literal: Whenever Ying and the others at court audience advanced congratulations, He always lowered his intent and received them with joy.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Ying and his fellows came to court to offer congratulations, Sun He always humbled himself and welcomed them warmly.

sentences.zh: 講校經義，綜察是非，及訪諮朝臣，考績行能，以知優劣，各有條貫。

translations.literal: He lectured and collated canonical meanings, comprehensively examined right and wrong, and when he visited and consulted court ministers, examined their conduct and ability so as to know excellence and inferiority, each having its systematic order.
translations.idiomatic: He discussed the Classics, weighed right and wrong, questioned ministers about policy, and assessed their performance so that merit and fault each had its place.

sentences.zh: 後諸葛壹僞叛以誘魏將諸葛誕，權潛軍待之。

translations.literal: Later Zhuge Yi feigned rebellion to lure the Wei general Zhuge Dan; Sun Quan secretly stationed troops awaiting him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhuge Yi pretended to defect to lure Zhuge Dan of Wei; Sun Quan hid an army to spring the trap.

sentences.zh: 和以權暴露外次，又戰者凶事，常憂勞憯怛，不復會同飲食，數上諫，戒令持重，務在全勝，權還，然後敢安。

translations.literal: He because Sun Quan was exposed in camp outside, and moreover warfare is an inauspicious matter, constantly worried and grieved in bitter distress, no longer joined in common drinking and eating, several times submitted remonstrance, enjoining him to be steady and weighty, striving for complete victory; only when Sun Quan returned did he dare be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: With his father camped in the field and war—a thing of ill omen—hanging over the state, Sun He could not bring himself to feast; he remonstrated again and again that Sun Quan hold steady and aim at total victory, and only when the sovereign returned did he rest easy.

sentences.zh: 張純字元基，敦之子。

translations.literal: Zhang Chun, courtesy name Yuanji, was the son of Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun, courtesy name Yuanji, was the son of Zhang Dun.

sentences.zh: 《吳錄》曰：純少厲操行，學博才秀，切問捷對，容止可觀。

translations.literal: The Wu lu states: Chun in youth hardened his conduct, his learning was broad and his talent outstanding, he pressed questions and answered swiftly, and his bearing was worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu lu records that Zhang Chun disciplined himself young, was widely read and talented, asked sharp questions and answered crisply, and carried himself with presence.

sentences.zh: 拜郎中，補廣德令，治有異績，擢爲太子輔義都尉。〉

translations.literal: He was appointed gentleman of the palace, supplemented as magistrate of Guangde, his rule had unusual traces of success, and he was promoted to capital commandant who aids righteousness for the heir. )
translations.idiomatic: He served as a gentleman of the palace, then as magistrate of Guangde with a distinguished record, and rose to capital commandant assisting the heir. )

sentences.zh: 是時有司頗以條書問事，和以爲姦妄之人，將因事錯意，以生禍心，不可長也，表宜絕之。

translations.literal: At that time the responsible officials often used written clauses to inquire into affairs; He considered that treacherous and reckless men would thereby twist intent according to events and give birth to a mind of disaster, and this could not be allowed to grow; he submitted a memorial that it ought to be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Officials had begun probing cases with written questionnaires. Sun He argued that schemers would twist such forms to stir trouble, and memorialized to abolish the practice.

sentences.zh: 又都督劉寶白庶子丁晏，晏亦白寶，和謂晏曰：「文武在事，當能幾人，因隙構簿，圖相危害，豈有福哉？

translations.literal: Again Area Commander Liu Bao denounced the palace attendant Ding Yan, and Yan in turn denounced Bao; He said to Yan: "Civil and military men in office—how many can there be? Because of cracks they construct ledgers, plotting to harm one another—how can there be blessing?"
translations.idiomatic: When Area Commander Liu Bao and palace attendant Ding Yan denounced each other, Sun He told Ding Yan, "How few men truly hold office! To nurse grudges and plot mutual ruin can only bring ruin on us all."

sentences.zh: 」遂兩釋之，使之從厚。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he released both sides and had them treat each other generously.
translations.idiomatic: " He freed both from the quarrel and urged them toward generosity.

sentences.zh: 常言當世士人宜講脩術學，校習射御，以周世務，而但交游博弈以妨事業，非進取之謂。

translations.literal: He constantly said that gentlemen of the age ought to lecture on and cultivate technical learning, drill and practice archery and charioteering, so as to complete affairs of the world, yet they only wandered in socializing and gaming at bo, hindering the enterprise—this was not what is called advancing and seizing.
translations.idiomatic: He often said scholars should study useful arts and drill riding and archery for practical affairs, not fritter life away in gaming and parties if they meant to accomplish anything.

sentences.zh: 後羣寮侍宴，言及博弈，以爲妨事費日而無益於用，勞精損思而終無所成，非所以進德脩業，積累功緒者也。

translations.literal: Later when the host of officials attended a banquet and talk touched on gaming at bo, he held that it hindered affairs and wasted days without benefit for use, taxed the spirit and injured thought yet in the end accomplished nothing—it was not the means by which to advance virtue and cultivate enterprise and pile up merit and continuity.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at a banquet with his officials, talk turned to bo. Sun He argued that it wasted time, drained the mind, and achieved nothing—that it was no way to build character or a career.

sentences.zh: 且志士愛日惜力，君子慕其大者，高山景行，恥非其次。

translations.literal: Moreover men of purpose love the day and treasure their strength; the gentleman admires the great in it—high mountains and bright conduct—and is ashamed not to be second to them.
translations.idiomatic: Men of purpose cherish time and strength; the gentleman looks to the highest example and is ashamed to fall short.

sentences.zh: 夫以天地長乆，而人居其間，有白駒過隙之喻，年齒一暮，榮華不再。

translations.literal: Now as heaven and earth are long enduring yet man dwells between them, there is the metaphor of the white colt passing the crevice; once the years turn toward evening, glory and splendor do not return.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth endure, but man's life flashes past like a white colt glimpsed through a crack—once youth is gone, splendor does not return.

sentences.zh: 凡所患者，在於人情所不能絕，誠能絕無益之欲以奉德義之塗，棄不急之務以脩功業之基，其於名行，豈不善哉？

translations.literal: Generally what one ought to worry over lies in what human feeling cannot cut off; if one can truly cut off unprofitable desires so as to devote oneself to the path of virtue and righteousness, cast aside unurgent tasks so as to cultivate the foundation of merit and enterprise, as to name and conduct, how could it not be good?
translations.idiomatic: Our worst enemy is appetite we cannot master. Cut useless desires to walk the path of honor, drop busywork to lay foundations for real achievement—could name and conduct be better served?

sentences.zh: 夫人情猶不能無嬉娛，嬉娛之好，亦在於飲宴琴書射御之間，何必博弈，然後爲歡。

translations.literal: Moreover human feeling still cannot be without amusement; the liking for amusement also lies among drinking feasts, zithers and books, archery and charioteering—why must there be gaming at bo, and only then be joy?
translations.idiomatic: Nor need we be grim: pleasure lives in feasts, music, books, riding, and archery—must we rely on dice to be happy?

sentences.zh: 乃命侍坐者八人，各著論以矯之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered the eight men seated in attendance each to compose a treatise to correct it.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore told the eight companions at his side each to write an essay refuting the habit.

sentences.zh: 於是中庶子韋曜退而論奏，和以示賔客。

translations.literal: Thereupon Palace Attendant Wei Yao withdrew and composed a memorial on it, and He showed it to guests.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Wei Yao then drafted a piece on the subject, which Sun He shared with his guests.

sentences.zh: 時蔡穎好弈，直事在署者頗斆焉，故以此諷之。

translations.literal: At the time Cai Ying loved playing yi; those on duty in the office quite imitated him; therefore he used this to admonish them.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Ying was fond of yi, and the clerks on duty had begun to imitate him—hence the pointed lesson.

sentences.zh: 是後王夫人與全公主有隙。

translations.literal: After this Lady Wang and the Princess of Quan had a rift.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Lady Wang and the Princess of Quan fell out.

sentences.zh: 權嘗寢疾，和祠祭於廟，和妃叔父張休居近廟，邀和過所居。

translations.literal: Sun Quan once lay ill with a sleeping sickness; He performed sacrifice and prayer in the temple; He's consort's paternal uncle Zhang Xiu dwelt near the temple and invited He to pass his dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan fell seriously ill, Sun He sacrificed at the ancestral temple. His consort's uncle Zhang Xiu lived nearby and asked the heir to stop at his house.

sentences.zh: 全公主使人覘視，因言太子不在廟中，專就妃家計議；

translations.literal: The Princess of Quan had people spy and watch, and on that account said the heir apparent was not in the temple but had gone specially to the consort's kin to plot counsel;
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Quan had him watched, then reported that the crown prince had skipped the temple to plot at his in-laws' house;

sentences.zh: 又言王夫人見上寢疾，有喜色。

translations.literal: she also said that when Lady Wang saw the sovereign lying ill with a sleeping sickness, she had a joyful expression.
translations.idiomatic: she added that Lady Wang had looked pleased when the sovereign took to his bed.

sentences.zh: 權由是發怒，夫人憂死，而和寵稍損，懼於廢黜。

translations.literal: Sun Quan for this reason gave vent to anger; the lady died in worry, and He's favor was gradually diminished; he feared deposition.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan exploded with rage. Lady Wang died of grief, Sun He's favor waned, and he began to fear deposition.

sentences.zh: 魯王霸覬覦滋甚，陸遜、吾粲、顧譚等數陳適庶之義，理不可奪，全寄、楊笁爲魯王霸支黨，譖愬日興。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu Ba gazed with ever greater covetousness; Lu Xun, Wu Can, Gu Tan, and others several times set forth the righteousness that separates heir and concubine's son, the principle being that it could not be wrested away; Quan Ji and Yang Zhu became partisan supporters of the Prince of Lu Ba, and slander and complaint rose daily.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sun Ba of Lu eyed the throne more openly. Lu Xun, Wu Can, and Gu Tan repeatedly argued the law of legitimate heir versus younger sons, but Quan Ji and Yang Zhu backed Sun Ba, and slander flew daily.

sentences.zh: 粲遂下獄誅，譚徙交州。

translations.literal: Can thereupon went down to prison and was executed; Tan was banished to Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Can was jailed and killed; Gu Tan was banished to Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 權沈吟者歷年，

translations.literal: Sun Quan hesitated for successive years,
translations.idiomatic: For years Sun Quan wavered,

sentences.zh: 〈殷基《通語》曰：初權旣立和爲太子，而封霸爲魯王，初拜猶同宮室，禮秩未分。

translations.literal: ( Yin Ji's Tong yu states: At first, after Sun Quan had established He as heir apparent and enfeoffed Ba as Prince of Lu, at first investiture they still shared the same palace quarters and ritual rank was not divided.
translations.idiomatic: ( Yin Ji's Tong yu records that when Sun He was made heir and Sun Ba prince of Lu, they at first still shared quarters and equal ceremony.

sentences.zh: 羣公之議，以爲太子、國王上下有序，禮秩宜異，於是分宮別僚，而隙端開矣。

translations.literal: The host of dukes' deliberation held that heir apparent and prince of the state, superior and inferior, had an order, and ritual rank ought to differ; thereupon they divided palaces and separated staffs, and the crack of rift opened.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers argued that crown prince and feudal prince must observe rank; separate households and staffs were ordered, and the split began.

sentences.zh: 自侍御賔客造爲二端，仇黨疑貳，滋延大臣。

translations.literal: From attendants, imperial companions, and guests they fashioned two ends; factions of enmity and suspicion in two minds spread and extended among great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants and guests chose sides; suspicion spread through the high ministers.

sentences.zh: 丞相陸遜、大將軍諸葛恪、太常顧譚、驃騎將軍朱據、會稽太守滕胤、大都督施績、尚書丁密等奉禮而行，宗事太子，驃騎將軍步隲、鎮南將軍呂岱、大司馬全琮、左將軍呂據、中書令孫弘等附魯王，中外官僚將軍大臣舉國中分。

translations.literal: Chancellor Lu Xun, Grand General Zhuge Ke, Grand Master of Ceremonies Gu Tan, Cavalry General Zhu Ju, Administrator of Kuaiji Teng Yin, Area Commander Shi Ji, Minister Ding Mi, and others upheld ritual and acted accordingly, making the heir apparent their clan concern; Cavalry General Bu Zhi, General Who Stabilizes the South Lü Dai, Grand Marshal Quan Zong, General of the Left Lü Ju, Director of the Secretariat Sun Hong, and others attached to the Prince of Lu; inner and outer clerks, generals, and great ministers split the whole state down the middle.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun, Zhuge Ke, Gu Tan, Zhu Ju, Teng Yin, Shi Ji, Ding Mi, and others stood by ritual and backed the heir; Bu Zhi, Lü Dai, Quan Zong, Lü Ju, Sun Hong, and others backed the Prince of Lu. The court and camp were torn in two.

sentences.zh: 權患之，謂侍中孫峻曰：「子弟不睦，臣下分部，將有袁氏之敗，爲天下笑。

translations.literal: Sun Quan worried over it and said to Palace Attendant Sun Jun: "The sons and younger brothers are not harmonious; the subordinates divide into factions—there will be the Yuan clan's defeat and We shall be laughed at by the world.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan told Sun Jun, "My sons feud and my servants take sides—we risk the Yuan brothers' disaster and the world's mockery.

sentences.zh: 一人立者，安得不亂？

translations.literal: When one man is established, how can there not be chaos?
translations.idiomatic: How can the realm stay calm when two heirs are in play?

sentences.zh: 」於是有改嗣之規矣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon there was a plan to change the successor.
translations.idiomatic: " He began to consider replacing the heir.

sentences.zh: 臣松之以爲袁紹、劉表謂尚、琮爲賢，本有傳後之意，異於孫權旣以立和而復寵霸，坐生亂階，自構家禍，方之袁、劉，昏悖甚矣。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that Yuan Shao and Liu Biao held Shang and Cong worthy and originally had intent to transmit the succession—this differed from Sun Quan, who having already established He again favored Ba, thereby sitting and producing the steps of disorder and for himself constructing family calamity; compared to Yuan and Liu, his benighted perversity was extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi comments: Yuan Shao and Liu Biao genuinely preferred their younger sons—unlike Sun Quan, who had already named an heir yet doted on Sun Ba, inviting ruin at home. Beside them Sun Quan looks far more blind.

sentences.zh: 步隲以德度著稱，爲吳良臣，而阿附於霸，事同楊笁，何哉？

translations.literal: Bu Zhi was famed for virtue and measure, was a good minister of Wu, yet he fawned and attached to Ba—the affair being the same as Yang Zhu's—how could it be?
translations.idiomatic: Bu Zhi was celebrated as a worthy Wu minister—why did he cling to Sun Ba like Yang Zhu?

sentences.zh: 和旣正位，適庶分定，就使才德不殊，猶將義不黨庶，況霸實無聞，而和爲令嗣乎？

translations.literal: He having already taken correct position, legitimate heir and concubine's son were divided and fixed; granting that talents and virtues were not different, still the righteousness would not favor the concubine's son—how much more when Ba in truth had no reputation, while He was the lawful successor?
translations.idiomatic: Once the rightful heir was fixed, the line between legitimate son and younger brother was clear. Even had their talents been equal, duty forbids siding with the lesser son—and Sun Ba had no reputation beside Sun He.

sentences.zh: 夫邪僻之人，豈其舉體無善，但一爲不善，衆美皆亡耳。

translations.literal: As for depraved and crooked men, how can their whole persons lack good?—yet once they do one ungood thing, all their beauties perish.
translations.idiomatic: A wicked man is not all vice—but one wrong act cancels every virtue.

sentences.zh: 隲若果有此事，則其餘不足觀矣！

translations.literal: If Zhi truly had this affair, then the rest is not worth viewing!
translations.idiomatic: If Bu Zhi really did that, nothing else he did deserves our respect!

sentences.zh: 呂岱、全琮之徒，蓋所不足論耳。〉

translations.literal: As for Lü Dai, Quan Zong, and their sort, they are probably not worth discussing. )
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dai, Quan Zong, and their like scarcely merit discussion. )

sentences.zh: 後遂幽閉和。

translations.literal: Afterward they thereupon confined He in seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Sun He was then placed under house arrest.

sentences.zh: 於是驃騎將軍朱據、尚書僕射屈晃率諸將吏泥頭自縛，連日詣闕請和。

translations.literal: Thereupon Cavalry General Zhu Ju, Vice Director of the Secretariat Qu Huang, leading the host of generals and clerks with mud on their heads and binding themselves, for successive days went to the palace gates requesting reconciliation for He.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ju and Vice Director Qu Huang led officers to the gates with heads smeared with mud and ropes on their wrists, day after day begging Sun Quan to forgive Sun He.

sentences.zh: 權登白爵觀見，甚惡之，勑據、晃等無事忩忩。

translations.literal: Sun Quan ascended the White Heron Watch and saw them; he greatly hated it and ordered Ju, Huang, and the others to have no business in frantic haste.
translations.idiomatic: From the White Heron Watch Sun Quan saw the demonstration and was furious; he ordered Zhu Ju and Qu Huang to stop their clamor.

sentences.zh: 權欲廢和立亮，無難督陳正、五營督陳象上書，稱引晉獻公殺申生，立奚齊，晉國擾亂，又據、晃固諫不止。

translations.literal: Sun Quan wished to depose He and establish Liang; the Colonel of the Garrison Without Difficulty Chen Zheng and the Colonel of the Five Camps Chen Xiang submitted memorials, citing Duke Xian of Jin who killed Shen Sheng and established Xi Qi, whereby Jin was thrown into turmoil; again Ju and Huang firmly remonstrated without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan meant to depose Sun He for Sun Liang, colonels Chen Zheng and Chen Xiang cited Duke Xian of Jin, who killed Crown Prince Sheng to install Xi Qi and threw the state into chaos; Zhu Ju and Qu Huang still would not let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 權大怒，族誅正、象，據、晃牽入殿，杖一百，

translations.literal: Sun Quan was greatly angry, exterminated the clans of Zheng and Xiang, dragged Ju and Huang into the hall, and caned them one hundred strokes,
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan raged, executed Chen Zheng and Chen Xiang root and branch, had Zhu Ju and Qu Huang dragged into court, and gave them a hundred strokes,

sentences.zh: 〈《吳歷》曰：晃入，口諫曰：「太子仁明，顯聞四海。

translations.literal: ( The Wu li states: When Huang entered, he remonstrated with his mouth: "The heir apparent is humane and enlightened, renowned within the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: ( The Wu li says Qu Huang entered and cried, "The crown prince is humane and wise, known throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 今三方鼎跱，實不宜搖動太子，以生衆心。

translations.literal: Now the three sides stand like tripods; it is truly not fitting to shake the heir apparent so as to give birth to the multitude's doubts.
translations.idiomatic: The three kingdoms stand like a tripod; you must not unsettle the heir and sow doubt among the people.

sentences.zh: 願陛下少垂聖慮，老臣雖死，猶生之年。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty slightly to let fall sagely consideration; though your aged servant die, it is still as the years of his life.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you reconsider—though this old minister die, he will count his life well spent.

sentences.zh: 」叩頭流血，辭氣不撓。

translations.literal: " He knocked his head until it bled; his words and temper did not bend.
translations.idiomatic: " He beat his head on the floor until the blood flowed and never softened his tone.

sentences.zh: 權不納晃言，斥還田里。

translations.literal: Sun Quan did not accept Huang's words and dismissed him to return to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan refused to hear him and sent Qu Huang home to his lands.

sentences.zh: 孫皓即位，詔曰：「故僕射屈晃，志匡社稷，忠諫亡身。

translations.literal: When Sun Hao assumed the throne, he issued an edict: "The former Vice Director of the Secretariat Qu Huang, his aim was to rectify the altars of soil and grain, and he loyally remonstrated unto death.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Hao came to the throne he decreed, "The late Vice Director Qu Huang gave his life in loyal remonstrance for the altars of state."

sentences.zh: 封晃子緒爲東陽亭侯，弟幹、恭爲立義都尉。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed Huang's son Xu as village marquis of Dongyang, younger brothers Gan and Gong as capital commandants who uphold righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed Qu Huang's son Qu Xu as village marquis of Dongyang and his brothers Qu Gan and Qu Gong as capital commandants for upholding righteousness.

sentences.zh: 」緒後亦至尚書僕射。

translations.literal: " Xu later also reached the office of Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: " Qu Xu later rose to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 晃，汝南人，見胡沖荅問。

translations.literal: Huang was a man of Runan; see Hu Chong's Questions and Answers.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Huang was from Runan; see Hu Chong's Questions and Answers.

sentences.zh: 《吳書》曰：張純亦盡言極諫，權幽之，遂棄市。〉

translations.literal: The Wu shu states: Zhang Chun also spoke exhaustively in extreme remonstrance; Sun Quan confined him, then cast him aside in the market. )
translations.idiomatic: The Wu shu adds that Zhang Chun remonstrated to the limit; Sun Quan jailed him and had him executed in the marketplace. )

sentences.zh: 竟徙和於故鄣，羣司坐諫誅放者十數。

translations.literal: In the end He was moved to Guchang; hosts of officials who sat for remonstrance were executed or banished in numbers of ten and more.
translations.idiomatic: Sun He was banished to Guchang, and a dozen or more officials who had pleaded for him were killed or exiled.

sentences.zh: 衆咸冤之。

translations.literal: The multitude all held it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion held him wronged.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：權寢疾，意頗感寤，欲徵和還立之，全公主及孫峻、孫弘等固爭之，乃止。〉

translations.literal: ( The Wu shu states: When Sun Quan lay ill with a sleeping sickness, his mind was quite moved to enlightenment and he wished to summon He back and establish him; the Princess of Quan and Sun Jun, Sun Hong, and others firmly contested it, and only then he stopped. )
translations.idiomatic: ( The Wu shu says that when Sun Quan fell ill he nearly recalled Sun He as heir, but the Princess of Quan and Sun Jun and Sun Hong blocked it. )

sentences.zh: 孫休立，封和子皓爲烏程侯，自新都之本國。

translations.literal: When Sun Xiu was established, he enfeoffed He's son Hao as marquis of Wucheng, who went from Xindu to his own state.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Xiu took the throne he enfeoffed Sun He's son Sun Hao as marquis of Wucheng, who traveled from Xindu to his fief.

sentences.zh: 休薨，皓即阼，其年追謚父和曰文皇帝，改葬明陵，置園邑二百家，令、丞奉守。

translations.literal: When Xiu died, Hao succeeded to the throne; that year he posthumously honored his father He with the title Emperor Wen, reburied him at Ming Mausoleum, established a park settlement of two hundred households, and ordered a magistrate and assistant to maintain guardianship.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Xiu died Sun Hao succeeded; the same year he posthumously titled his father Sun He as Emperor Wen, reinterred him at Ming Mausoleum with a two-hundred-household funerary estate under magistrate and assistant.

sentences.zh: 後年正月，又分吳郡、丹楊九縣爲吳興郡，治烏程，置太守，四時奉祠。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, again he divided nine counties of Wu commandery and Danyang to make Wu commandery of Xing, administering Wucheng, and established a grand administrator, with seasonal sacrifice in four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: The next New Year he carved nine counties from Wu and Danyang into a new Wu Xing commandery based at Wucheng, appointed a grand administrator, and ordered sacrifices each season.

sentences.zh: 有司奏言，宜立廟京邑。

translations.literal: The responsible officials submitted saying that a temple ought to be established in the capital city.
translations.idiomatic: Officials memorialized for an ancestral temple in the capital.

sentences.zh: 寶鼎二年七月，使守大匠薛珝營立寢堂，號曰清廟。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Baoding, he ordered the Guardian Grand Engineer Xue Xu to build a hall for the resting spirit, styled the Pure Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of 267 he had Guardian Grand Engineer Xue Xu build a spirit hall styled the Pure Temple.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遣守丞相孟仁、太常姚信等備官寮中軍步騎二千人，以靈輿法駕，東迎神於明陵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he sent Acting Chancellor Meng Ren, Grand Master of Ceremonies Yao Xin, and others with full complement of officials and followers, two thousand foot and horse of the central army, with the spirit carriage and statutory equipage, to go east and welcome the spirit at Ming Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he sent Acting Chancellor Meng Ren, Grand Master Yao Xin, a full retinue, and two thousand guards with the imperial bier east to Ming Mausoleum to fetch the spirit.

sentences.zh: 皓引見仁，親拜送於庭。

translations.literal: Hao led Ren in audience and personally bowed in sending off at the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao received Meng Ren in audience and bowed him off in the courtyard himself.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：比仁還，中使手詔，日夜相繼，奉問神靈起居動止。

translations.literal: ( The Wu shu states: When Ren returned, inner envoys with autograph edicts succeeded one another day and night, conveying inquiries after the spirit's rest and rise, movement and stillness.
translations.idiomatic: ( The Wu shu says that while Meng Ren was returning, couriers with the emperor's own edicts followed one another night and day asking after the spirit's progress.

sentences.zh: 巫覡言見和被服，顏色如平生日，皓悲喜涕淚，悉召公卿尚書詣闕門下受賜。〉

translations.literal: Witches and shamans said they saw He in robes and caps, his complexion as on ordinary days of life; Hao was moved between joy and sorrow to tears and mucus, and summoned all dukes, ministers, and directors of departments to the gates below the palace to receive bestowal. )
translations.idiomatic: Mediums claimed Sun He appeared in court dress, his face as in life; Sun Hao wept for joy and sorrow and summoned the high ministers to the gate to receive blessings. )

sentences.zh: 靈輿當至，使丞相陸凱奉三牲祭於近郊，皓於金城外露宿。

translations.literal: When the spirit carriage was about to arrive, he ordered Chancellor Lu Kai to offer the three sacrificial victims in sacrifice at the near suburbs, while Hao lodged in the open outside the Metal Wall.
translations.idiomatic: As the bier neared, he told Chancellor Lu Kai to sacrifice the three victims in the near suburb while he himself camped in the open outside the Metal Wall.

sentences.zh: 明日，望拜於東門之外。

translations.literal: The next day he gazed and bowed outside the eastern gate.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he bowed toward the east outside the city gate.

sentences.zh: 其翌日，拜廟薦祭，歔欷悲感。

translations.literal: The day after that he bowed in the temple, presented sacrifice, sighed and wept, moved and grieved.
translations.idiomatic: The following day he worshiped at the temple, offered sacrifice, and wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 比七日三祭，倡技晝夜娛樂。

translations.literal: For seven days with three sacrifices, singing girls and performers by day and night provided entertainment.
translations.idiomatic: For seven days and three services, musicians and dancers entertained without cease.

sentences.zh: 有司奏言「祭不欲數，數則黷，宜以禮斷情」，然後止。

translations.literal: The responsible officials submitted saying "Sacrifice ought not to be frequent; if frequent then it is profane; one ought to cut off feeling by ritual"—only then did it stop.
translations.idiomatic: Officials cited the rule that frequent sacrifice is profane and urged ritual to curb excess—only then did the displays end.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳歷》曰：和四子：皓、德、謙、俊。

translations.literal: ( The Wu li states: He had four sons: Hao, De, Qian, and Jun.
translations.idiomatic: ( The Wu li lists four sons of Sun He: Sun Hao, Sun De, Sun Qian, and Sun Jun.

sentences.zh: 孫休即位，封德錢唐侯，謙永安侯，俊拜騎都尉。

translations.literal: When Sun Xiu assumed the throne, he enfeoffed De as marquis of Qiantang, Qian as marquis of Yongan, and Jun was appointed cavalry commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Xiu came to the throne he enfeoffed Sun De at Qiantang, Sun Qian at Yongan, and appointed Sun Jun cavalry commandant.

sentences.zh: 皓在武昌，吳興施但因民之不堪命，聚萬餘人，劫謙，將至秣陵，欲立之。

translations.literal: When Hao was at Wuchang, Shi Dan of Wu Xing, because the people could not bear their commands, gathered more than ten thousand men, seized Qian, and was about to reach Moling, intending to establish him.
translations.idiomatic: While Sun Hao was at Wuchang, Shi Dan of Wu Xing, claiming the people could not endure his rule, raised over ten thousand men, seized Sun Qian, and marched on Moling intending to enthrone him.

sentences.zh: 未至三十里住，擇吉日，但遣使以謙命詔丁固、諸葛靚。

translations.literal: Before reaching thirty li they halted, chose an auspicious day, but only sent envoys with Qian's order to summon Ding Gu and Zhuge Jing.
translations.idiomatic: They halted thirty li short, picked an auspicious day, and sent envoys in Sun Qian's name to summon Ding Gu and Zhuge Jing.

sentences.zh: 靚即斬其使。

translations.literal: Jing thereupon beheaded his envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Jing beheaded the messenger at once.

sentences.zh: 但遂前到九里，固、靚出擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Dan thereupon advanced to Jiuli; Gu and Jing came out and attacked, greatly defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dan pushed on to Jiuli; Ding Gu and Zhuge Jing sallied forth and crushed him.

sentences.zh: 但兵裸身無鎧甲，臨陣皆披散。

translations.literal: But Dan's soldiers were naked without armor; facing battle they all let their hair hang loose.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dan's men fought stripped of armor, hair streaming loose.

sentences.zh: 謙獨坐車中，遂生獲之。

translations.literal: Qian alone sat in a carriage; thereupon he was captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qian alone sat in a carriage and was taken alive.

sentences.zh: 固不敢殺，以狀告皓，皓酖之，母子皆死。

translations.literal: Gu did not dare kill him but reported the situation to Hao; Hao poisoned him with ale, and mother and son both died.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Gu dared not execute him and reported to Sun Hao, who poisoned him with wine; mother and son both died.

sentences.zh: 俊，張承外孫，聦明辨惠，爲遠近所稱，皓又殺之。〉

translations.literal: Jun was Zhang Cheng's maternal grandson, clever in discrimination and quick in wisdom, praised by far and near, and Hao again killed him. )
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jun was Zhang Cheng's grandson by a daughter—clever and praised far and wide—and Sun Hao killed him too. )

sentences.zh: 孫霸字子威，和弟也。

translations.literal: Sun Ba, courtesy name Ziwei, was He's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ba, styled Ziwei, was Sun He's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 和爲太子。

translations.literal: He was heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Sun He held the position of crown prince.

sentences.zh: 霸爲魯王，寵愛崇特，與和無殊。

translations.literal: Ba was Prince of Lu; favor and love were exalted and singular, no different from He.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ba was Prince of Lu, yet Sun Quan showered him with favor that matched the heir apparent in every outward respect.

sentences.zh: 頃之，和、霸不穆之聲聞於權耳，權禁斷往來，假以精學。

translations.literal: Before long the sound that He and Ba were not harmonious reached Sun Quan's ears; Sun Quan forbade and cut off their mutual visits, under the excuse of concentrated study.
translations.idiomatic: Word soon reached Sun Quan that the two brothers were estranged; he barred them from visiting each other, citing the need for diligent study.

sentences.zh: 督軍使者羊衜上疏曰：「臣聞古之有天下者，皆先顯別適庶，封建子弟，所以尊重祖宗，爲國藩表也。

translations.literal: Military overseer Yang Dao submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that those who possessed the realm in antiquity all first clearly distinguished heir and younger sons by birth, enfeoffed sons and younger brothers—thereby to honor the ancestors and be fence and outward model for the state."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dao, the army inspector, memorialized: "The ancients who ruled always drew a clear line between heir and younger sons and enfeoffed cadet princes—to honor the ancestors and ring the state with loyal kin."

sentences.zh: 二宮拜授，海內稱宜，斯乃大吳興隆之基。

translations.literal: When the two palaces received investiture, within the seas it was called fitting—this was the foundation of Great Wu's flourishing rise.
translations.idiomatic: The dual investiture won approval across the realm; it was the bedrock on which Wu could prosper.

sentences.zh: 頃聞二宮並絕賔客，遠近悚然，大小失望。

translations.literal: Recently your servant has heard that both palaces have altogether cut off guests; far and near are fearful, great and small disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Now both establishments have shut their doors to visitors; the whole country is uneasy and every rank is dismayed.

sentences.zh: 竊從下風，聽採衆論，咸謂二宮智達英茂，自正名建號，於今三年，德行內著，美稱外昭，西北二隅，乆所服聞。

translations.literal: Your servant has privately followed the leeward side, listened and gathered the multitude's discussions—all say the two palaces are wise, comprehensive, outstanding, and lush; since rectifying names and establishing titles, down to now three years, virtue and conduct have shown within, fair praise has shone without, and the two corners northwest have long submitted and heard.
translations.idiomatic: From what people say, both princes are gifted; three years since their titles were fixed, their virtue is known at home and their repute abroad—Wei and Shu have long taken note.

sentences.zh: 謂陛下當副順遐邇所以歸德，勤命二宮賔延四遠，使異國聞聲，思爲臣妾。

translations.literal: They say Your Majesty ought to answer and comply with what far and near rely on for returning virtue, diligently order the two palaces as guests to extend to the four distances, so that foreign states hearing the report will wish to become subjects and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: You should answer the hopes that bind the realm to you: bid both princes receive guests from every quarter so that rival states hear of their virtue and wish to submit.

sentences.zh: 今旣未垂意於此，而發明詔，省奪備衞，抑絕賔客，使四方禮敬，不復得通，雖實陛下敦尚古義，欲令二宮專志於學，不復顧慮觀聽小宜，期於溫故博物而已，然非臣下傾企喁喁之至願也。
