translations.literal: Now that you have not yet let fall intent on this but have issued a clarifying edict, reducing and taking away full guard, suppressing and cutting off guests, so that ritual respect from the four quarters can no longer get through—though in truth Your Majesty earnestly esteems ancient meaning and wishes the two palaces to fix their intent on study alone, no longer heed trifles of sight and hearing, aiming only at reviewing the old and broadly knowing things—yet it is not the utmost hope to which your subordinates incline and look upward with upturned mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Instead you have published an edict that strips their guards and bars their guests, so envoys can no longer pay court. You may mean only to keep them at their books, but your servants had hoped for something very different.

sentences.zh: 或謂二宮不遵典式，此臣所以寢息不寧。

translations.literal: Some say the two palaces do not follow canonical models—this is why your servant cannot sleep or rest in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Some already whisper that the two princes flout precedent—that is what keeps your servant awake at night.

sentences.zh: 就如所嫌，猶宜補察，密加斟酌，不使遠近得容異言。

translations.literal: Even granting the suspicions, still one ought to remedy and examine, secretly add weighing and deliberation, and not allow far and near to harbor different words.
translations.idiomatic: Even if those suspicions were true, you should investigate quietly and not let rumor find a foothold anywhere.

sentences.zh: 臣懼積疑成謗，乆將宣流，而西北二隅，去國不遠，異同之語，易以聞達。

translations.literal: Your servant fears that accumulated doubt will become slander, and in time it will spread and flow; while the two corners northwest are not far from the state, words of sameness and difference easily reach clarity.
translations.idiomatic: I fear doubt will curdle into slander and spread; our northern neighbors lie close—whispers travel fast.

sentences.zh: 聞達之日，聲論當興，將謂二宮有不順之愆，不審陛下何以解之？

translations.literal: When the day of reaching clarity comes, voices and opinions will surely rise; they will say the two palaces have faults of disobedience—your servant does not know how Your Majesty will explain it?
translations.idiomatic: When those rumors break surface, men will say both princes are disloyal—how will you answer them?

sentences.zh: 若無以解異國，則亦無以釋境內。

translations.literal: If there is no means to explain to foreign states, then there is also no means to release doubt within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot satisfy foreign courts, you cannot quiet your own people either.

sentences.zh: 境內守疑，異國興謗，非所以育巍巍，鎮社稷也。

translations.literal: Within the borders holding doubt, foreign states raising slander—this is not the means by which to nurture loftiness and stabilize the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: A doubtful populace and a mocking abroad are no way to nurture majesty or secure the altars.

sentences.zh: 願陛下早發優詔，使二宮周旋禮命如初，則天清地晏，萬國幸甚矣。」

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty early to issue a generous edict, so that the two palaces may go about ritual commands as at first—then heaven will be clear and earth tranquil, and within the myriad regions all will be fortunate in the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Issue a generous edict, I beg you, and let both princes receive guests and observe ceremony as before—then heaven and earth will be at peace and the realm will rejoice.

sentences.zh: 時全寄、吳安、孫奇、楊笁等陰共附霸，圖危太子。

translations.literal: At that time Quan Ji, Wu An, Sun Qi, Yang Zhu, and others secretly together attached to Ba and plotted to endanger the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Ji, Wu An, Sun Qi, Yang Zhu, and others secretly backed Sun Ba and plotted against the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 譖毀旣行，太子以敗，霸亦賜死。

translations.literal: When slander and destruction had gone forward, the heir apparent thereby failed; Ba also was ordered to die by bestowal.
translations.idiomatic: Slander did its work: the crown prince fell, and Sun Ba too was condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 流笁屍于江，兄穆以數諫戒笁，得免大辟，猶徙南州。

translations.literal: Zhu's corpse was floated in the river; his elder brother Mu because he several times remonstrated and warned Zhu, was spared the great execution, yet still was moved to the southern province.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhu's body was cast into the river. His brother Yang Mu, who had often warned him, escaped execution but was banished to the south.

sentences.zh: 霸賜死後，又誅寄、安、奇等，咸以黨霸搆和故也。

translations.literal: After Ba was ordered to die by bestowal, again Ji, An, Qi, and others were executed—all because they had factionally attached to Ba and framed He.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Ba's death, Quan Ji, Wu An, Sun Qi, and the rest were put to death for plotting with him against Sun He.

sentences.zh: 孫奮字子揚，霸弟也，母曰仲姬。

translations.literal: Sun Fen, courtesy name Ziyang, was Ba's younger brother; his mother was called Lady Zhongji.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fen, styled Ziyang, was Sun Ba's younger brother; his mother was Lady Zhongji.

sentences.zh: 太元二年，立爲齊王，居武昌。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiyuan he was established as Prince of Qi and dwelt at Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In 252 he was made Prince of Qi with his seat at Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 權薨，太傅諸葛恪不欲諸王處江濵兵馬之地，徙奮於豫章。

translations.literal: When Sun Quan died, Grand Tutor Zhuge Ke did not wish the kings to dwell in places of troops and horses along the riverbank, and moved Fen to Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Quan's death, Grand Tutor Zhuge Ke, unwilling to leave princes on the Yangzi garrison line, transferred Sun Fen to Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 奮怒，不從命，又數越法度。

translations.literal: Fen was angry, would not obey the order, and several times overstepped the laws and measures.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fen refused the order in fury and repeatedly broke the regulations.

sentences.zh: 恪上牋諫曰：「帝王之尊，與天同位，是以家天下，臣父兄，四海之內，皆爲臣妾。

translations.literal: Ke submitted a note remonstrating: "The honor of emperors and kings shares position with Heaven; therefore they treat the realm as family, and fathers and elder brothers among subjects are subjects and concubines; within the four seas all are subjects and concubines."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke sent him a written remonstrance: "The Son of Heaven shares rank with Heaven; the empire is his household, and every subject is his servant."

sentences.zh: 仇讎有善，不得不舉，親戚有惡，不得不誅，所以承天理物，先國後身，蓋聖人立制，百代不易之道也。

translations.literal: In foes there is good—you cannot fail to promote it; among kin there is evil—you cannot fail to execute it; by this one receives Heaven's pattern and orders things, putting the state first and the self after—this is the way the sage kings established institutions, the path unchanged for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Even an enemy's merit must be rewarded; even a kinsman's crime must be punished—that is how sages align with Heaven, put the state before private feeling, and set norms for all ages.

sentences.zh: 昔漢初興，多王子弟至於太彊，輒爲不軌，上則幾危社稷，下則骨肉相殘，其後懲戒，以爲大諱。

translations.literal: At the rise of Han in early times there were many kings among sons and younger brothers until they became too strong, then acted contrary to the track—above they nearly endangered the altars of soil and grain, below flesh and bone slew one another; afterward taking warning, they made it a great taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Early Han princes grew too strong, nearly toppled the dynasty, and turned on one another; later emperors took warning and kept royal power on a short leash.

sentences.zh: 自光武以來，諸王有制，惟得自娛於宮內，不得臨民，干與政事，其與交通，皆有重禁，遂以全安，各保福祚。

translations.literal: From Guangwu onward the kings had regulations: they might only amuse themselves within the palace, might not oversee the people or meddle in government affairs; their dealings with others had heavy prohibitions—thereby they were wholly secure, each preserving blessing and fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Since Guangwu, princes were confined to their palaces, barred from governing commoners or state affairs, and their contacts were strictly limited—so they lived out their lives in safety.

sentences.zh: 此則前世得失之驗也。

translations.literal: This is the verification of gain and loss in former ages.
translations.idiomatic: That is the lesson of history.

sentences.zh: 近袁紹、劉表各有國土，土地非狹，人衆非弱，以適庶不分，遂滅其宗祀。

translations.literal: Recently Yuan Shao and Liu Biao each had a state territory, their lands not narrow, their populations not weak—because heir and concubine's son were not divided, thereupon their ancestral sacrifices were extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao and Liu Biao held broad lands and large armies, yet because they blurred the line between heir and younger son they lost their houses.

sentences.zh: 此乃天下愚智，所共嗟痛。

translations.literal: This is what the foolish and wise of the world together sigh in pain over.
translations.idiomatic: Wise and simple alike still mourn that lesson.

sentences.zh: 大行皇帝覽古戒今，防芽遏萌，慮於千載。

translations.literal: The late emperor surveyed antiquity and guarded the present, nipped buds and stopped sprouts, thinking a thousand years ahead.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor read history, foresaw trouble, and cut princely power at the root for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 是以寢疾之日，分遣諸王，各早就國，詔策殷勤，科禁嚴峻，其所戒勑，無所不至，誠欲上安宗廟，下全諸王，使百世相承，無凶國害家之悔也。

translations.literal: Therefore on the days when he lay ill he separately dispatched the kings, each to go early to his state; edicts and patents were earnest, statutes and prohibitions strict and severe, what he warned and charged left nothing undone—truly he desired above to secure the ancestral temples, below to preserve the kings in full, so that a hundred generations would inherit in succession without the regret of a state harmed and house ruined.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he sent every prince to his fief with stern edicts and tight rules—wanting to secure the temples above and the royal kin below for ages to come.

sentences.zh: 大王宜上惟太伯順父之志，中念河間獻王、東海王彊恭敬之節，下當裁抑驕恣荒亂以爲警戒。

translations.literal: The great king ought above to ponder Taibo's intent to yield to his father, in the middle recall the moderation of Prince Xian of Hejian and Prince Qiang of the Eastern Sea, below ought to restrain arrogance, self-indulgence, wastefulness, and disorder and take them as warning.
translations.idiomatic: You should look upward to Taibo's yielding spirit, inward to the restraint of Han's virtuous princes, and downward to the warning of pride and license.

sentences.zh: 而聞頃至武昌以來，多違詔勑，不拘制度，擅發諸將兵治護宮室。

translations.literal: But your servant has heard that since you recently arrived at Wuchang you have often disobeyed edicts and charges, not kept to regulations, and on your own authority mobilized the generals' troops to build and guard the palace chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since you reached Wuchang you have defied orders, ignored statute, and called up troops on your own authority to fortify your residence.

sentences.zh: 又左右常從有罪過者，當以表聞，公付有司，而擅私殺，事不明白。

translations.literal: Again when those at your right and left who constantly follow had faults and crimes, you ought to have reported them in a memorial and handed them over to the responsible officials, yet you on your own privately killed them—the affair was not made clear.
translations.idiomatic: When attendants broke the law you should have reported them to the proper offices; instead you executed them privately without due process.

sentences.zh: 大司馬呂岱親受先帝詔勑，輔導大王，旣不承用其言，令懷憂怖。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Lü Dai personally received the late emperor's edicts and charges to instruct and guide the great king; you have not accepted and employed his words, causing him to harbor worry and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Lü Dai bears the late emperor's mandate to guide you; your refusal to heed him has left him in fear for his life.

sentences.zh: 華錡先帝近臣，忠良正直，其所陳道，當納用之，而聞怒錡，有收縛之語。

translations.literal: Hua Qi was a close minister of the late emperor, loyal, good, and straight; what he set forth in the way ought to be accepted and employed—yet your servant has heard you were angry at Qi and had words of arresting and binding him.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Qi was a trusted upright minister of the late sovereign; you should heed him—yet you are said to have threatened him with arrest.

sentences.zh: 又中書楊融，親受詔勑，所當恭肅，云『正自不聽禁，當如我何』？

translations.literal: Again Palace Writer Yang Rong personally received edicts and charges—what he ought to have been was reverent and solemn—yet your servant has heard he said, "If I simply will not listen to the prohibition, what can he do to me?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rong of the Secretariat received the same charge to keep you in line, yet he is said to have sneered, "If I ignore the rules, what can anyone do about it?"

sentences.zh: 聞此之日，大小驚怪，莫不寒心。

translations.literal: When the day your servant heard this, great and small were startled and strange, none did not feel cold at heart.
translations.idiomatic: When these words spread, every rank in the capital shuddered.

sentences.zh: 里語曰：『明鏡所以照形，古事所以知今。

translations.literal: A village saying goes: "The bright mirror is what shows form; old affairs are what let one know the present.
translations.idiomatic: The proverb runs, "The bright mirror reflects the face; old stories illumine the present."

sentences.zh: 』大王宜深以魯王爲戒，改易其行，戰戰兢兢，盡敬朝廷，如此則無求不得。

translations.literal: " The great king ought deeply to take the Prince of Lu as a warning, change and alter his conduct, tremble with fear, exhaust reverence toward the court—if so then nothing sought will not be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: " Take the Prince of Lu as your mirror: mend your ways, walk in fear, and show perfect deference to the court, and you may yet obtain all you seek."

sentences.zh: 若棄忘先帝法教，懷輕慢之心，臣下寧負大王，不敢負先帝遺詔，寧爲大王所怨疾，豈敢忘尊主之威，而令詔勑不行於藩臣邪？

translations.literal: If you cast aside and forget the late emperor's laws and instruction and harbor a mind of slight contempt, your subordinates would rather wrong the great king than dare wrong the late emperor's testamentary charge; they would rather be resented and hated by the great king than dare forget the awesome authority of the honored ruler and let edicts and charges not be carried out on a vassal minister!
translations.idiomatic: If you spurn the late emperor's teaching and grow arrogant, we would rather offend you than betray his final charge; we would rather earn your hatred than let your defiance of the throne go unchecked!

sentences.zh: 此古今正義，大王所照知也。

translations.literal: This is the orthodox righteousness of past and present, what the great king illumines and knows.
translations.idiomatic: That is the justice every age acknowledges, and you know it as well as we do.

sentences.zh: 夫福來有由，禍來有漸，漸生不憂，將不可悔。

translations.literal: Fortune comes with a cause, calamity comes with a gradualness; if gradual growth is not worried over, there will be no chance for regret.
translations.idiomatic: Blessing and disaster do not strike overnight; ignore the first steps and there will be no mending them later.

sentences.zh: 向使魯王早納忠直之言，懷驚懼之慮，享祚無窮，豈有滅亡之禍哉？

translations.literal: Suppose the Prince of Lu had early taken loyal and straight words, harbored a mind of alarm and fear—would he not have enjoyed blessing without end—how could there have been the calamity of extinction?
translations.idiomatic: Had the Prince of Lu heeded loyal counsel and lived in fear, he might still enjoy his fief—would he have perished as he did?

sentences.zh: 夫良藥苦口，惟疾者能甘之。

translations.literal: Good medicine is bitter in the mouth—only the sick can deem it sweet.
translations.idiomatic: Good medicine tastes bitter—only the patient welcomes it.

sentences.zh: 忠言逆耳，惟達者能受之。

translations.literal: Loyal words grate on the ear—only the comprehending can receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal words grate—only the wise accept them.

sentences.zh: 今者恪等慺慺欲爲大王除危殆於萌芽，廣福慶之基原，是以不自知言至，願蒙三思。」

translations.literal: Now Ke and the others anxiously desire for the great king to remove peril and danger at the sprouting, broaden the foundation of blessing and fortune—therefore they are not aware that their words have reached the utmost; they wish to receive your thrice pondering.
translations.idiomatic: We urge you in fear and loyalty to root out danger while it is still a sprout and widen the base of your fortune; we have spoken bluntly—please weigh our words three times.

sentences.zh: 奮得牋懼，遂移南昌，游獵彌甚，官屬不堪命。

translations.literal: Fen received the note and was afraid; thereupon he moved to Nanchang, and his roaming hunts became extreme; his officials could not bear the commands.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fen took fright, moved to Nanchang, and hunted so relentlessly that his staff could not endure his demands.

sentences.zh: 及恪誅，奮下住蕪湖，欲至建業觀變。

translations.literal: When Ke was executed, Fen came down and stopped at Wuhu, intending to go to Jianye to observe the change.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuge Ke's execution Sun Fen encamped at Wuhu, intending to march on Jianye and watch how events unfolded.

sentences.zh: 傅相謝慈等諫奮，奮殺之。

translations.literal: Tutor Xie Ci and others remonstrated Fen; Fen killed them.
translations.idiomatic: His tutors Xie Ci and others tried to dissuade him; he put them to death.

sentences.zh: 〈慈字孝宗，彭城人，見《禮論》，撰《喪服圖及變除》行於世。〉

translations.literal: ( Ci, courtesy name Xiaozong, was a man of Pengcheng; see his Lun on Rites, and he composed Diagrams of Mourning Garb and Removal, which circulated in the world. )
translations.idiomatic: ( Xie Ci, styled Xiaozong, came from Pengcheng; he wrote on ritual and compiled a work on mourning dress that circulated widely. )

sentences.zh: 坐廢爲庶人，徙章安縣。

translations.literal: For his crime he was degraded to commoner and moved to Zhang'an county.
translations.idiomatic: He was reduced to commoner status and banished to Zhang'an county.

sentences.zh: 太平三年，封爲章安侯。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping he was enfeoffed as marquis of Zhang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In 258 he was restored as marquis of Zhang'an.

sentences.zh: 〈《江表傳》載亮詔曰：「齊王奮前坐殺吏，廢爲庶人，連有赦令，獨不見原，縱未宜復王，何以不侯？

translations.literal: ( The Jiangbiao zhuan records Liang's edict: "Prince of Qi Fen earlier sat in the crime of killing officials and was degraded to commoner; successive amnesties have come, yet alone he was not forgiven—even if it is not yet fitting to restore him as king, why not make him a marquis?
translations.idiomatic: ( Sun Liang's edict in the Jiangbiao zhuan reads: "Sun Fen killed officials and was stripped of rank; though amnesties have passed him by, he should at least be a marquis again if not a prince."

sentences.zh: 又諸孫兄弟作將，列在江渚，孤有兄獨爾云何？

translations.literal: Again among the grandsons and brothers who serve as generals, arrayed along the river isles, I alone have an elder brother—how can it be thus?
translations.idiomatic: "My royal cousins command troops along the river—why should my elder brother alone lack a noble title?"

sentences.zh: 」有司奏可，就拜爲侯。〉

translations.literal: " The responsible officials memorialized approval; thereupon he was invested as marquis on the spot. )
translations.idiomatic: " The ministry approved, and he was invested as marquis. )

sentences.zh: 建衡二年，孫皓左夫人王氏卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianheng, Sun Hao's left consort Lady Wang died.
translations.idiomatic: In 270 Sun Hao's senior consort Lady Wang died.

sentences.zh: 皓哀念過甚，朝夕哭臨，數月不出，由是民間或謂皓死，訛言奮與上虞侯奉當有立者。

translations.literal: Hao's grief and longing were excessive; morning and evening he wept at the bier, for several months did not go out; for this reason among the people some said Hao had died, and false rumor said Fen and Feng the marquis of Shangyu ought to be the ones established.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao mourned so wildly that for months he never left the palace; rumor spread that he was dead and that Sun Fen or Sun Feng might seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 奮母仲姬墓在豫章，豫章太守張俊疑其或然，掃除墳塋。

translations.literal: Fen's mother Lady Zhongji's tomb was in Yuzhang; the administrator of Yuzhang Zhang Jun suspected it might be so, and swept and cleared the grave mound.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fen's mother was buried in Yuzhang; Administrator Zhang Jun, thinking the rumor might be true, cleaned her tomb as though Sun Fen were already sovereign.

sentences.zh: 皓聞之，車裂俊，夷三族，誅奮及其五子，國除。

translations.literal: When Hao heard it, he had Jun torn apart by carts, exterminated three clans, executed Fen and his five sons, and abolished the state.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao had Zhang Jun torn apart by carts, wiped out three generations of his kin, executed Sun Fen and his five sons, and abolished the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 〈《江表傳》曰：豫章吏十人乞代俊死，皓不聽。

translations.literal: ( The Jiangbiao zhuan states: Ten clerks of Yuzhang begged to die in Jun's place; Hao would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: ( Ten Yuzhang clerks offered to die in Zhang Jun's stead; Sun Hao refused. )

sentences.zh: 奮以此見疑，本在章安，徙還吳城禁錮，使男女不得通婚，或年三十四十不得嫁娶。

translations.literal: Fen for this was suspected; originally he was at Zhang'an, was moved back to Wucheng city and imprisoned, so that men and women could not intermarry, some reaching thirty or forty years without being able to marry.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fen fell under suspicion. Though he had lived at Zhang'an, he was confined in Wucheng city; men and women of his household were forbidden to marry, and some reached thirty or forty unwed.

sentences.zh: 奮上表乞自比禽獸，使男女自相配偶。

translations.literal: Fen submitted a memorial begging to compare himself to birds and beasts, letting men and women mate among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fen begged leave to be treated like beasts—at least allowed to breed among themselves.

sentences.zh: 皓大怒，遣察戰齎藥賜奮，奮不受藥，叩頭千下，曰：「老臣自將兒子治生求治，無豫國事，乞丐餘年。

translations.literal: Hao was greatly angry, sent an inspector of war to bring poison and bestow it on Fen; Fen would not accept the poison, knocked his head a thousand times, saying: "Your aged servant will lead his sons in seeking livelihood and order—he has nothing to do with state affairs; I beg the leavings of years."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao sent an officer with poison. Sun Fen refused it, kowtowed a thousand times, and cried that he only wished to live out his days in private obscurity with his sons.

sentences.zh: 」皓不聽，父子皆飲藥死。

translations.literal: " Hao would not listen; father and sons all drank the drug and died.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Hao was unmoved; father and sons were forced to drink the poison and died.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案：建衡二年至奮之死，孫皓即位，尚猶未乆。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers: from the second year of Jianheng to Fen's death, Sun Hao's assumption of the throne was still not long.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes: from 270 to Sun Fen's death Sun Hao had not reigned long.

sentences.zh: 若奮未被疑之前，兒女年二十左右，至奮死時，不得年三十四十也。

translations.literal: If before Fen was suspected the sons and daughters were about twenty in years, by the time of Fen's death they could not have reached thirty or forty.
translations.idiomatic: If his children were about twenty when he first fell under suspicion, they could not all have been thirty or forty when he died.

sentences.zh: 若先已長大，自失時未婚娶，則不由皓之禁錮矣。

translations.literal: If they had earlier already grown large and on their own missed the season of being unwed and unmarried, then it was not because of Hao's imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: Any who were already of age and still unmarried before the confinement cannot be blamed on Sun Hao's policy alone.

sentences.zh: 此雖欲增皓之惡，然非實理。〉

translations.literal: This although it wishes to increase Hao's evil, yet is not solid principle. )
translations.idiomatic: ( The tale piles Sun Hao's cruelty higher than the facts allow. )

translations.literal: 【Appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 評曰：孫登居心所存，足爲茂美之德。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: What Sun Deng stored in his heart was enough to be luxuriant and beautiful virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser says: Sun Deng's inner life was the stuff of true nobility.

sentences.zh: 慮、和並有好善之姿，規自砥礪，或短命早終，或不得其死，哀哉！

translations.literal: Lu and He together had the bearing that loves the good; they regulated and sharpened themselves—some met early death with short fate, some did not obtain natural death—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lü and Sun He both loved the good and strove to better themselves—one died young, the other was destroyed; how pitiful!

sentences.zh: 霸以庶干適，奮不遵軌度，固取危亡之道也。

translations.literal: Ba by a concubine's son meddled with the heir; Fen did not follow track and measure—solidly they took the path of danger and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ba, a younger son, muscled against the heir; Sun Fen scorned the rules—each courted ruin by a clear road.

sentences.zh: 然奮之誅夷，橫遇飛禍矣。

translations.literal: Yet Fen's execution and extermination met calamity that flew from nowhere.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Sun Fen's slaughter was sheer mischance, a bolt from the blue.
